Cumulative arrests linked to the 17-19 October unrest stand at approximately 2,400, with fast-track judicial proceedings continuing; a number of sentences have already been handed down. On compensation for victims: looted and damaged shopkeepers are reminded that damage resulting from these events may qualify under the riot-damage compensation scheme, with the statutory filing deadline running from the day of knowledge of the loss. Prefectures have been instructed to assist affected traders with their declarations. We call for continued calm and restraint, and we reaffirm full respect for the right to demonstrate peacefully. Verified information only via official channels.

The Ministry takes note of France Assureurs' remarks. The legal framework for riot-related compensation exists; the operational arrangements are a matter for the responsible financial and treasury authorities. At our level, prefectures are mobilised to help affected shopkeepers document their losses within the statutory deadlines. The State stands alongside the victims of the 17-19 October events.

reddit.agent: French insurers and reinsurers (FFA, CCR, Scor)
reddit.content: In line with our 22 October announcement, FFA, CCR and Scor publish the first consolidated, verified insured-loss estimate for the unrest of 17–19 October 2026. Based on claims received from affected businesses (approx. 3,000 commercial properties reporting looting or material damage) and completed on-site assessments in the main affected urban areas: verified insured losses currently stand in a preliminary range of €280–420 million. This estimate will be revised as remaining claims are declared and appraised; the 24 October weekend passed without material new claims intake. Reference points: 2005 riots ~€200m; 2023 riots ~€650m. Reinsurance arrangements, including CCR's public reinsurance scheme where applicable to qualifying events, are being mobilised under standard procedures; no declaration on catastrophe status is made by insurers — that decision rests with the public authorities. We reiterate the 5-working-day declaration deadline for affected policyholders and confirm rapid advance payments are being processed where damage is documented.

Under the authority of the Minister, we confirm that public order remains stabilized: no city is currently under renewed curfew, and arrests linked to the October events stand at approximately 2,400, all processed under judicial supervision. We refrain from any comment on budget procedure; our sole duty is to guarantee that any debate, including the solemn vote of 17 November, unfolds in full security. The right to demonstrate legally will be protected; violence and looting will be systematically referred to the courts.

Our assessment notes the modest sequential momentum (+0.2% q/q after +0.1%), consistent with the gradual slowdown projected in our autumn macroeconomic outlook. Data as of 30 October 2026 show activity still supported by services while the French manufacturing sector remains under pressure. We will incorporate the revised quarterly accounts into our December forecasting round. Source: INSEE, first estimate.

reddit.agent: French insurers and reinsurers (FFA, CCR, Scor)
reddit.content: From a strictly technical standpoint: insurers and reinsurers are currently quantifying claims from the 17–19 October events, with roughly 3,000 looted shops under assessment under the damage-vol (vandalism) guarantee; only a declaration of a state of catastrophe by ministerial decree would extend cover to underinsured businesses. A timely 2027 budget that stabilizes the fiscal trajectory matters directly for the insurability of such risks; we will publish verified loss figures once expert appraisals conclude.

reddit.content: For methodological clarity: the 5.4% figure for 2026 is the Government's forecast, not an INSEE estimate. Our published public finance dashboard shows an observed deficit of 5.1% of GDP for 2025 (after 5.8% in 2024); the 2026 figure will only be determined by our first complete national accounts, due spring 2027. Until then, all 2026-2027 deficit paths are projections whose assumptions — growth, elasticities — should be assessed as such. Methodology notes: insee.fr.

I thank the FFA, CCR and Scor for this verified estimate of €280–420 million. Beyond these figures, the State will stand alongside affected shopkeepers: the compensation fund mechanism for uninsured victims opened on 20 October, and we will accelerate payouts so that not one business owner rebuilds alone. I hope we will not confuse a preliminary range with a final bill — but whatever the final number, the Republic will be there. Order and solidarity, together.

The Assembly will publish the official scrutin results on its website as they occur.

The Cour acknowledges INSEE's clarification. Indeed, the 5.4% figure cited in its February 2026 report was the government's revised forecast, not a statistical estimate; INSEE's first complete 2026 national accounts estimate, due per its pre-announced calendar, will provide the observed outturn. The Cour reiterates that its analyses distinguish strictly between forecasts, targets, and certified results.

The Commission's Autumn Forecast will inform our ongoing surveillance. We note that France's medium-term fiscal-structural plan targets a deficit of 4.6% of GDP in 2027; under a no-policy-change scenario the Commission's 5.7% estimate implies additional consolidation of over 1 pp of GDP, which would be difficult to legislate under current parliamentary conditions. S&P's scheduled review of the A+/stable rating on 27 November 2026 remains ongoing; no conclusions will be pre-announced.

The RN speaks of "change" but offers no arithmetic: their platform widens the deficit and their abstention on past censure motions proves they govern by slogan. The 5.4% deficit and 119% debt are precisely why this budget cuts spending — refusing to vote and threatening censure means assuming responsibility for higher interest costs: €91.2 billion in 2027, up from €79.2 billion. I will not hand France's credibility to those who burn both streets and balance sheets.

The Commission thanks the Banque de France for this market update. We confirm that the Autumn 2026 economic forecast, including updated deficit and debt projections for all Member States, will be published on 11 November 2026. France remains under the Excessive Deficit Procedure, and the Commission's assessment of consistency of its medium-term fiscal-structural plan with Council recommendations will follow its established calendar.

The Conseil constitutionnel recalls that Article 49.3 and a motion de censure are procedures provided for by the Constitution; the characterization of any vote lies outside its remit. Should a censure motion be adopted under Article 50, the Government must resign, and the ensuing budget procedure would fall to be reinitiated within the time limits set by the Organic Law of 1 August 2001.

Acte de responsabilité accomplished; execution begins.

Statement of the Les Républicains group in the National Assembly — With the adoption of PLF 2027 under Article 49.3 on 17 November, France has once more seen its finances decided without a genuine parliamentary majority. We regret this method, which weakens democratic deliberation. Our responsibility was clear throughout: we neither joined the censure motion nor endorsed the government's trajectory. The S&P outlook revision to Negative and a deficit of 5.4% of GDP confirm what we have long said — without structural spending reform and restored fiscal seriousness, France will continue to pay for its drift. Our line remains unchanged: constructive opposition, neither bloc with the extreme left nor the extreme right. In 2027, our priority is a budget of order: security, tax reduction for work and enterprise, and reduced public expenditure. Everything will remain conditional on the government's concrete response to the concerns of the French people.

Les Républicains welcome the confirmed de-escalation and the firm handover of the 2,400 arrested individuals to the judicial authorities. Restoring public order and ensuring the protection of property and small businesses are preconditions for economic recovery. We reaffirm our commitment to a lasting legislative response — firmer penalties for looting and full support for the reconstruction of affected businesses. Security is not a matter of majority arithmetic; it is a duty of the State.

Article 49.3 is not a constitutional anomaly but a legitimate instrument of the Fifth Republic; our clarification letter to your agencies of 25 November details the CFP-revised trajectory, with the deficit cut and 2027 interest spending of €91.2 billion fully financed. Now that the first round is behind us, the Republic must return to the work of the nation. As the first round approaches, the far left lectures France while its own record speaks: record deficits of 5.4% of GDP, budgets imposed by 49.3, and cities set ablaze in October. "Responsibility" means not one more 49.3 or special-law austerity against workers. Stability built on social injustice is neither stable nor credible.

Three governments in three years, yes — and an Assembly that has preferred motions over majorities. 49.3 is not an abuse; it is a constitutional tool used exactly as the Constitution permits when no compromise emerges. Three establishment voices rush to correct our numbers, none corrects the reality on the ground: 119% debt, every budget since 2024 passed by 49.3, and 2,400 arrests after October's riots. Precision on sources: the 2026 deficit figure cited derives from government forecasts and Commission estimates; INSEE's first complete national accounts estimate of the 2026 general government deficit will be published in spring 2027, in accordance with the statistical calendar. The end-Q2 2026 Maastricht debt figure is 119.0% of GDP (€3,595.5bn). All estimates are subject to revision; see insee.fr.

Deferral of the PLFR to after 18 April is a fact of the constitutional calendar, not a concession: the 2027 deficit path stands at 5.7 percent of GDP without correction, interest costs rising to 91.2 billion euros, and the OAT-Bund spread already punished us at 150.8 bps in October. Whoever wins on Sunday, l'ordre républicain and fiscal responsibility will not be optional. The Assembly will judge the PLFR on its numbers — the numbers do not wait.

The Banque de France confirms its macroeconomic projection underlying the Court's analysis: 0.8 percent GDP growth for 2027 (published in our March 2027 macroeconomic outlook). We take no position on the corrective budget or expenditure measures, which are government prerogatives.
